x: It must have been quite a bind for our Adrian Major (5th last year) knowing that he was quite capable of giving one or both of these a fright, had he been fitter. Peter Blair-Fish was our second man home, followed closely by the rest of our team but too far back to get near the medals.

We fielded teams in the Youth and Junior races but as we are particularly weak in these classes at the present time there is little to be said except that Peter Blair-Fish who finished 108th in the Junior race ran reasonably well.
Second and third prizes went to Peter Blair-Fish, who is showing steady improvement, and George Piddington - obviously the sea air agrees with him.
John Blair-Fish, Peter's younger brother, produced personal best performances recently when he recorded 4:45.2 for the mile and 10:06 for 2 miles.

Making a welcome visit south over the Christmas period was JOHN BLAIR-FISH who led our small team home over at Blackheath. On Boxing Day he teamed up with his brother PETER and sister to enter the Chipstead Pram Race and finished a worthy second behind one JOHN THRESHER.
… a senior, Dave McMillan (12) - now fighting back from terrible injuries sustained while out training and hit by a car, P.Blair-Fish (46).…
